This convention is so ingrained that violating it feels disorienting. 00225| 00226| Use the `transitionTypes` prop on `` to tag forward navigations: 00227| 00228| ```tsx filename="components/photo-grid.tsx" 00229| 00230| {/* photo thumbnail */} 00231| 00232| ``` 00233| 00234| The same pattern works for any navigation within the app. For example, previous/next arrows on a photo detail page can use `nav-back` and `nav-forward` to animate in the corresponding direction. 00235| 00236| For links that return the user to a previous page, use `nav-back`: 00237| 00238| ```tsx filename="app/photo/[id]/page.tsx" 00239| 00240| ← Gallery 00241| 00242| ``` 00243| 00244| The transition type is not automatic. A sliding header breaks the user's spatial anchor. They need one fixed reference point to understand that the _content_ moved, not the entire viewport. 00332| 00333| Assign the header a `viewTransitionName` and suppress its animation in CSS: 00334| 00335| ```tsx filename="components/header.tsx" 00336|

If we click the "← Gallery" link (tagged with `nav-back`), content slides right. The header stays fixed throughout both transitions. 00357| 00358| Browser-initiated back navigations (the back button or swipe gestures) do not carry a transition type, so the directional slide does not play. It feels like switching content within the same container. 00394| 00395| A directional slide would be wrong here. Slides communicate "going to a new place." The container persists (continuity), only the grid inside changes (swap). 00396| 00397| Use a `ViewTransition` with `key` set to the current slug. ---
title: Designing view transitions
description: Learn how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation, loading, and content changes in a Next.js app.
nav_title: View transitions
---

In web apps, route changes replace the entire page at once. One set of elements disappears, another appears, with no visual connection between them. A user selects a photo thumbnail to view it in detail on another page. They are the same image, but nothing on screen communicates that.

Apps that need these transitions typically rely on complex animation libraries that manage mount/unmount lifecycles, track element positions across routes, and coordinate timing manually, to animate how elements enter, exit, and move between states.

React's `<ViewTransition>` component integrates with the browser's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) to handle this declaratively. You name the elements that should persist, and the browser animates between their old and new positions.

This guide walks through four patterns that cover the most common cases: morphing shared elements, animating loading states, adding directional navigation, and crossfading content within the same route.

## Add view transitions with an agent

The [`vercel-react-view-transitions`](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/vercel-react-view-transitions) skill teaches a coding agent the patterns in this guide, plus the CSS recipes and troubleshooting for applying them to an existing app.

Install the skill:

part.text:
Done. Uses React's `<ViewTransition>` (bundled with Next 16 canary, no config needed):

- **Shared element morph**: `ViewTransition name={\`product-${slug}\`} share="morph"` wraps both the grid thumbnail (`app/ProductGrid.tsx:13`) and detail hero (`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:58`), so the image animates between thumbnail and hero in both directions.
- **Directional slides**: links carry `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` / `['nav-back']`, and each page wraps its content in a `ViewTransition` mapping those types to `nav-forward`/`nav-back` slide classes. Browser back button (no type) still morphs without sliding.
- **Suspense reveals**: fallbacks get `exit="slide-down"`, content gets `enter="slide-up"` on both pages; `default="none"` everywhere prevents animations on unrelated transitions.
- **Reduced motion**: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroes all view-transition durations/delays and disables the skeleton pulse (`app/globals.css:210`).

Added `react-canary.d.ts` for `react/canary` types. `next build` passes; smoke test confirms the named transition elements render.
